title: Sadhna Rai v. Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
disposition: Writ disposed of: restore supply on deposit of ₹7,83,705 within three weeks; remaining dues to a clause 6.5 application.
headnote: On the parties' statements, the Allahabad High Court disposed of a billing-and-disconnection writ by directing the consumer to deposit ₹7,83,705 within three weeks, upon which the disconnected supply would be restored, and by leaving remaining dues to an application before respondent No. 2 (clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005) to be decided in accordance with law. The Court did not examine whether the bill was exorbitant.
facts: Sadhna Rai challenged Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. over an alleged exorbitant electricity bill and disconnection. The petitioner said at least ₹7,83,705 was demanded, COVID-19 losses had left the petitioner unable to pay, and that sum would be deposited within three weeks if a fresh demand issued for the balance. The distribution company agreed that deposit of ₹7,83,705 would restore supply and a fresh demand would follow. Respondent No. 3 submitted that remaining dues could be taken to respondent No. 2 under clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

holding_units.topic: restoration on deposit; remaining bill to clause 6.5
holding_units.holding: The writ was disposed of on the parties' statements: the petitioner was directed to deposit ₹7,83,705 within three weeks, and on that deposit the disconnected connection would be restored. Remaining dues were left to an appropriate application before respondent No. 2 — counsel having pointed to clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 — who may pass an appropriate order in accordance with law. The Court did not examine whether the bill was exorbitant.

principle_tags.application: Remaining dues after the consented deposit were left to a clause 6.5 application before respondent No. 2 rather than being decided on the writ.
Counsel for respondent No. 3 pointed to a clause 6.5 application before respondent No. 2; the Court adopted that course for the remaining amount.

not_decided.point: Whether the bill was exorbitant and what sum remained due
not_decided.note: Left to an application before respondent No. 2 under clause 6.5, to be decided in accordance with law.
